entries.title: Name participant roles in each of your event's languages
entries.summary: On a multi-language event, every participant role, including the ones your team created, has **Language variants**: a singular and plural name for each language. Reviewers, submitters and speakers who pick that language see it on the Review portal (cards, **Print all**, the submission page), in the submission form's participant roles and on the speaker portal's Participants tab. A language left blank shows the role's own name.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Roles → ⋯ Edit → Language variants

entries.use_case: An association running its review in Spanish and French can show “Autor presentador” and “Coautor” to Spanish reviewers instead of the English role names.

cs_action.note: Nothing switches on by itself: role names have to be typed per language in Program → Settings → Roles. For a multi-language customer whose reviewers see English role chips, walk them through adding the names for their custom roles. Track names are set separately, on the Track field's Language variants.

internal.gotchas: Shows only on events with more than one language. Track names are not edited here; they are option translations on the Track field. Speaker, Chairperson and Moderator already read in Spanish, French and German while they keep their original names; a role's own variant overrides that.
internal.staff_path: Program → Settings → Roles → ⋯ Edit → Language variants (event must have more than one language under Settings → Event Details → Supported Languages)
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers and speakers now see your own role names, like Presenting author and Co-author, in their language.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A multi-language customer reports role names (Presenting author, Co-author, …) in English in the Review portal, the submission form or the speaker portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with more than one event language, especially medical and scientific societies reviewing abstracts in several languages.

entries.title: Awards and Interest Form videos stream, and file questions take drag and drop
entries.summary: File questions on Awards nomination forms and Interest Forms (session and speaker questions, signed in or not) now upload straight to Sessionboard: drag a file onto the box or choose one, up to 5 GB. A video entry gets a copy made for streaming (up to 720p) a minute or two after upload, so reviewers in Awards review and the Review portal watch it without long pauses; **Download** always gives the original. Files your team adds from the submission sheet work the same way.

where.path: Awards → program → Submissions → open an entry → click a video (or the reviewer's portal → My Reviews → open an entry)

entries.use_case: An awards program that collects video entries can let reviewers watch them straight through instead of waiting for a large original to buffer.

cs_action.note: Automatic for files uploaded after this release. Entries uploaded before keep playing and downloading as they were (they are on Filestack's CDN and cannot get a streaming copy). HTML and SVG uploads are refused; prod had none on Awards or Interest Forms.

internal.gotchas: A video opened within a minute or two of upload may still play the original while its copy is made. Light videos that already stream well play as uploaded, with no note. The upload limit is 5 GB a file.
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Submissions → open an entry with a video → click the video
internal.talk_track: Video entries now stream for your reviewers, and Download still gives the full-quality original.
internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer launching a video entry category, or reporting Awards reviewers seeing videos pause or load slowly.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with video categories, and Interest Form customers who collect sizzle reels or session videos.
